Source-project MATLAB behavior, graphics, global root scans and arbitrary analytic continuation.
preconditions: Density returns finite real numeric scalar samples; the Cauchy integral exists on the selected contour.

Caller bounds or mesh resolve all material density features; whole-line tails are integrable and contain no unresolved density features. The integrator resolves the known kernel peak without requiring the caller to mesh the pole-height scale.
supported: Finite ordered bounds already resolving the callback support.
Whole-line integration with an explicit finite increasing integration_mesh that resolves support/features and integrable tails.

example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_cauchy_transform
mesh=np.linspace(-10,10,81)
r=evaluate_cauchy_transform(0.4+0.7j,lambda v: np.exp(-v*v)/np.sqrt(np.pi),integration_mesh=mesh)
assert np.isfinite(r["G"])
example.expected: A finite complex transform and two component error estimates.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for invalid, nonfinite, singular or incompatible inputs, including epsabs/epsrel=None or non-scalar values and callback-only whole-line integration without integration_mesh.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Raises RuntimeError if any QUADPACK panel reports nonconvergence; no partial result is returned.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial scientific result is returned after a failed call.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Callback exceptions propagate; invalid callback output or unrepresentable result raises ValueError.

assumptions: The callback is finite on every integrated panel.
For bounds=null, integration_mesh explicitly partitions material support/features and the two tails are integrable.
A generic callback cannot certify unseen density support from adaptive samples; the known Cauchy kernel scale is handled internally. Error estimates remain conditional.
identity.coordinates: Complex phase point and real integration coordinate
identity.definition: For z=x+i*y, near-projection finite panels use v=x+abs(y)*sinh(t), giving density(v)*(tanh(t)+i*sign(y)*sech(t)) dt. Bounded transformed panels resolve the known kernel peak and long tails; smooth far panels and infinite tails use real-coordinate quadrature. Explicit analytic continuation is added only under the stated support policy.

inputs.description: Complex phase points off the real axis.
inputs.name: z

inputs.constraints: Callable returning finite real numeric scalars at all sampled velocities; caller declares feature resolution.
inputs.description: Real density callback of one real velocity.
inputs.name: density

inputs.constraints: None selects whole-line mode with required mesh; otherwise finite ordered real pair; booleans and complex coordinates rejected.
inputs.name: bounds

inputs.constraints: Strictly increasing finite points; with bounds, mesh must lie inside bounds. When bounds is null, mesh endpoints delimit a resolved feature region and infinite tails are also integrated.
inputs.description: Finite strictly increasing real mesh partitioning material support/features; required when bounds is null.
inputs.name: integration_mesh
inputs.shape: one-dimensional array with at least two points

inputs.constraints: None or callable returning finite numeric scalars, representing the analytic extension of the same density. Finite-bound continuation only for strict a < Re(z) < b.

inputs.name: analytic_density

outputs.description: Summed real/imaginary quadrature indicators with floating accumulation allowances, including continuation; not bounds on callback or analytic-extension errors.

python.signature: evaluate_cauchy_transform(z, density, *, bounds=None, analytic_density=None, epsabs=1e-10, epsrel=1e-10, limit=200, integration_mesh=None)

summary: Evaluate a Cauchy transform with kernel-aware near-axis quadrature and caller-resolved density features.

verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent constant/affine finite-support logarithmic antiderivatives cover both half-planes, pole heights from1 to1e-300, endpoint/interior/exterior cases and multi-point shape; Gaussian special-function and Lorentzian residue identities cover whole-line tails. These numerical regressions support the kernel transformation, not arbitrary callback feature discovery or a certified global error bound.
known_limitations: A finite interval truncates any tail not represented by caller bounds; whole-line mode requires caller-supplied mesh/support resolution and assumes integrable tails.
Component indicators include quadrature and floating accumulation estimates but exclude callback, analytic-extension and finite-domain truncation errors; they are not global certificates.
Analytic continuation requires an explicit analytic callback matching the density.
scope: Independent analytic finite-interval identities and component error reporting.
Explicit feature-mesh whole-line shifted Gaussian cases with independent Faddeeva references.
Failure closure for callback-only whole-line support and malformed tolerances.
Known near-real-axis kernel peaks and logarithmic-scale tails are resolved independently of density feature mesh; strict finite-support continuation endpoint policy is retained.
